data.name: Ghoulboy - Dark Sword of Goblin
data.detailed_description:
Try Beholgar!


Acerca do jogo

Ghoulboy is a retro-inspired style action platformer. Exciting new platformer that combines the action-RPG genre with hack 'n' slash gameplay. 2D action, heroic characters, gloomy environments, demonic bosses, these all seem to excite players a lot. Pixels will be combined with other cool retro elements and the result will certainly be something that will meet the needs of PC gamers. Once in-game, users will get to control a heroic character who will often be seen throwing a spear to create additional platforms. To boot, puzzle and combat elements will further enhance the experience. You wouldn’t want to miss out on it. With the gold that you collect, you can increase your health level, your arsenal of weapons to be thrown away.
Slay as many monsters as you can, collect loot, avoid dangerous traps and defeat menacing bosses.
Ghoulboy brings back the look and feel of the very best classic retro platformers from the 90's, introducing refreshed and engaging gameplay mechanics. If you miss platformers from the 16-bit era, and think games nowadays aren't that good anymore, think twice! Ghoulboy is for you.
​GHoulboy Features:
-4 bosses
-Chiptune retro musics
-Puzzles
-3 weapons (small sword,big sword, mace)
-2 throwable weapons
-Gamepad support

A GREAT ADVENTURE• Explore a magical realm of dungeons, towns, treasures and devious monsters.
MAGIC AND SWORDS• Find powerful weapons, items and spells to defeat your enemies.

reviews.review:
Ghoulboy - Dark Sword of Goblin is a charming retro-inspired action-platformer that captures the adventurous spirit of classic 16-bit gaming while incorporating elements of hack-and-slash combat, exploration, and light role-playing progression. Developed and published by Serkan Bakar, the game presents a fantasy adventure filled with dangerous monsters, mysterious dungeons, hidden treasures, and challenging platforming sequences. Its straightforward gameplay and nostalgic presentation make it an appealing experience for players who appreciate traditional side-scrolling adventures. Although it does not attempt to revolutionize the genre, its combination of familiar mechanics and creative environmental interactions provides an enjoyable foundation for an old-school action game.

The adventure follows a heroic warrior traveling through a magical world populated by hostile creatures, treacherous obstacles, and powerful enemies. Rather than emphasizing complicated storytelling or extensive dialogue, the experience focuses on exploration, combat, and overcoming environmental challenges. Players encounter gloomy locations, dangerous dungeons, and settlements while collecting valuable resources and discovering equipment. This relatively simple narrative structure complements the game's arcade-inspired identity, allowing the action to remain the central attraction. However, those expecting elaborate character development or an emotionally engaging storyline may find the narrative comparatively limited.

Combat revolves around traditional melee attacks supported by throwable weapons. Players can utilize three primary weapons, consisting of a small sword, a larger sword, and a mace. These options provide some flexibility when confronting different enemies, although the overall combat system remains deliberately uncomplicated. Success depends on positioning, timing attacks, and avoiding incoming damage rather than mastering elaborate combinations or advanced combat techniques. The hack-and-slash mechanics create an accessible experience that encourages players to concentrate on defeating monsters and surviving increasingly hazardous encounters. Nevertheless, the limited weapon selection may eventually feel restrictive for those accustomed to more sophisticated action RPGs.

One of the game's most distinctive features involves throwing spears to create additional platforms. This clever mechanic transforms an ordinary offensive tool into an essential environmental resource, introducing an interesting relationship between combat equipment and exploration. Players can use strategically placed spears to reach elevated areas, overcome obstacles, and navigate otherwise inaccessible sections. The mechanic adds a welcome puzzle-solving dimension to traditional platforming, encouraging experimentation and thoughtful movement. It also provides the game with a recognizable gameplay feature that distinguishes it from more conventional retro adventures.

Exploration is supported by collectible treasures, useful equipment, and opportunities to improve the protagonist's capabilities. Gold collected throughout the adventure can be used to increase health and enhance throwable weapon capacity, introducing a modest sense of progression. These upgrades reward players for gathering resources and provide practical benefits during difficult encounters. The game also advertises magical items and spells, reinforcing its fantasy setting. However, its role-playing mechanics remain relatively lightweight, offering straightforward improvements rather than extensive customization, branching skill trees, or complicated character-building systems.

Environmental challenges contribute significantly to the overall experience. Dangerous traps, platforming obstacles, enemy encounters, and occasional puzzles create variety as players progress through the fantasy world. The emphasis on precise movement and careful observation reflects the design philosophy of traditional action-platformers. Four advertised boss encounters provide additional challenges and serve as important milestones throughout the adventure. While these confrontations strengthen the sense of progression, their relatively small number may disappoint players seeking a more extensive collection of memorable boss battles.

Visually, Ghoulboy embraces colorful pixel graphics combined with gloomy fantasy environments. Its character designs, monsters, and atmospheric locations evoke the appearance of classic console adventures without relying on demanding graphical technology. The retro presentation establishes a consistent identity that complements the gameplay's straightforward mechanics. Chiptune music further strengthens the nostalgic atmosphere, providing an appropriate soundtrack for exploration and combat. Although the audiovisual presentation lacks the technical sophistication of modern productions, its traditional aesthetic remains one of the game's defining attractions.

The experience also benefits from its accessibility and modest technical requirements. Full controller support makes it particularly suitable for players who prefer traditional gamepad controls, while its lightweight graphics allow it to accommodate relatively basic computer hardware. Steam achievements provide additional objectives for completionists, although the overall experience remains focused on single-player progression. Its uncomplicated design makes it approachable for newcomers, while the platforming challenges offer enough resistance to appeal to experienced genre enthusiasts.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game currently carries an Unknown classification, meaning Valve has not officially confirmed it as Verified or Playable. Its full controller support, modest hardware requirements, and traditional 2D gameplay suggest that it could be suitable for handheld gaming. However, successful operation through SteamOS and Proton cannot be guaranteed without further testing. Players interested in experiencing the adventure on Steam Deck should therefore consider compatibility unverified and remain prepared for possible configuration adjustments.

Despite its appealing qualities, the game has limitations. Its relatively small arsenal, straightforward combat mechanics, modest progression system, and limited boss selection restrict its overall depth. Players seeking an expansive Metroidvania, elaborate RPG systems, or extensive narrative content may find the experience insufficiently ambitious. Nevertheless, these shortcomings are balanced by an accessible gameplay structure, creative spear-based platforming, nostalgic audiovisual design, and a satisfying emphasis on traditional action-adventure fundamentals.

Overall, Ghoulboy - Dark Sword of Goblin offers an enjoyable tribute to classic side-scrolling fantasy adventures. Its strongest qualities lie in its retro atmosphere, accessible combat, rewarding exploration, and inventive environmental mechanics. While its simplicity and limited mechanical variety prevent it from reaching the heights of more ambitious platformers, it remains a worthwhile choice for players seeking a straightforward nostalgic adventure filled with monsters, treasures, puzzles, and challenging obstacles.

Rating: 7/10
